_comment: CONTINUATION sweep, run with: uv run python scripts/train_campaign.py --sweep sweep_recipe.json [--dry-run]. Two entries, in order: (1) a FORK of the transformer v0.62.0 at its peak 30k checkpoint onto a wsd anneal, landing as a NEW folder (next free minor, v0.63.0); (2) a RESUME of the GRU v0.41.0 from 240k to 500k on cosine. WHAT CHANGED FROM THE PREVIOUS REVISION: run 1 was 'tf-v0.59-to-120k-48x4', an 8-10h resume finishing the 12.03M transformer; it is DROPPED and replaced by the fork -- full reasoning in that run's own _comment, in short the size ladder is spent (no trend over 7.2x parameters), the resume would re-run the cosine recipe that costs ~130 Elo, and no continuation can lift v0.59.0's pinned max_seq=512. Before that revision, the three RECIPE-RECOVERY transformer arms were removed as done: arm 0 reached its horizon (v0.60.0 @90k), arm 2 ran as v0.61.0, arm 3 as v0.62.0. Their verdict is what run 1 now builds on -- the batch-64 regression was the COSINE SCHEDULE, not batch size (v0.57.0 cosine 685 vs v0.60.0 constant 814, same body), and the sqrt(2) lr scaling is load-bearing at batch 64 (v0.61.0, identical to v0.60.0 but lr 1e-4, peaks 601 @20k then decays to 547). NOTE v0.61.0 stopped at 60k of its 90k horizon; it is deliberately NOT re-added, since run 1 owns the box. If you want it finished later, add {"resume": "v0.61.0", "overrides": {"train.total_iters": 90000, "train.async_actors": 48, "train.actor_games": 4, "train.drain_per_cycle": 256, "train.traj_queue_size": 2048}} -- v0.61.0 is lr_schedule=constant so its horizon can be restated without distorting the curve. THE 'defaults' BLOCK BELOW IS STILL INERT: train_campaign.py:304 layers 'defaults' onto FRESH runs only, and there are none here -- a resume replays its own version's pinned checkpoints/v*/config.json (pinned_flat, train_campaign.py:178) and a FORK replays the SOURCE version's (train_campaign.py:366), in both cases with this file's 'overrides' on top. It is kept verbatim as the pinned record of the 1.67M transformer body so a fresh arm can be appended without re-deriving it; if you do append one, note train.async_actors=56 there was never actually run (every arm overrode it to 48, which is what fits the 60-vCore VM alongside the learner's own threads), and that its network.* block is the 1.67M body -- a fresh d384 scaling arm would override mixer_dim/mixer_layers/nhead and inherit max_seq 1024 for free. NO 'tournament' SECTION, ON PURPOSE, unchanged: it disables the per-run gauntlet and keep_top pruning, saving ~45-60 min per run and keeping every checkpoint. Enter the results on the ladder afterwards with: uv run python tools/tournament.py --worker 6 --model v0.63.0 (and again for v0.41.0).

runs._comment: RUN 1 -- FORK v0.62.0 at its PEAK checkpoint (30k) and anneal, testing whether the transformer's late-training collapse is an lr problem. WHAT THIS REPLACES: the previous revision queued 'tf-v0.59-to-120k-48x4', an 8-10h resume of the 12.03M v0.59.0 to its 120k horizon. It is DROPPED, not deferred. Reason: the size ladder it belongs to is already spent -- v0.57.0 1.67M = 673, v0.58.0 4.49M = 594, v0.59.0 12.03M = 624 at 80k xstep, no trend across 7.2x parameters -- and finishing it would re-run the batch-64 COSINE recipe that runs 1-3 of the previous revision showed costs ~130 Elo, on the arm with the stalest data of all (4.95x reuse, because a 12M model makes the CPU actors slow). It would also stay pinned at network.max_seq=512, which no resume can lift (train_campaign.py:309-314 rejects network.*/encoding.* on a continuation; weights are shape-locked), leaving the 'sequence length 513 exceeds max_seq 512' assert at network.py:232/241/249 live for the whole run. If the d384 body is ever worth another look, run it FRESH on this file's 'defaults' (which already carry max_seq 1024) with only mixer_dim/mixer_layers/nhead overridden -- ~7.6h for 60k steps, no warm-start confound, no assert. THE DEFECT THIS ARM TARGETS: v0.62.0 rises to 842 @30k, then does not hold it -- 819, 787, 790, 793, 801 across 40k-80k, then 685 @90k. Its metrics show why the last window falls apart: policy_loss swings between -1.0 and +2.1 step-to-step over the final ~3k steps (89,250: -0.994; 89,999: +1.819; 90,000: +2.073) while entropy stays flat at ~3.35, i.e. late instability, not entropy collapse. v0.42.0 has the same signature one batch size down (817 @100k -> 709 @240k). WHY wsd AND NOT cosine: cosine is what broke v0.57.0, but that was cosine-from-zero decaying THROUGH the learning phase; wsd holds the peak lr and anneals only after lr_decay_start, so it cannot damage the 0-30k rise that already happened. lr_decay_start is set to 30000 = the fork step, so annealing begins immediately at the fork and runs to lr_min=1e-5 at 90k: lr_at_step (trainer.py:71-79) takes decay_start=lr_decay_start for wsd, giving frac=(step-30000)/60000 and a smooth 1.4142e-4 -> 1e-5 cosine tail. WHY FORK AT 30k RATHER THAN RESUME AT 90k: the 90k weights are already inside the unstable regime the arm is trying to avoid; 30k is the strongest checkpoint on the ladder for this body. The fork's step counter starts at the SOURCE checkpoint's step (train_campaign.py:361-378 passes --resume <ckpt> and stamps train.fork_source), so the wsd curve is measured on absolute steps and the arithmetic above holds as written. NOTHING NEEDS RESTATING HERE, unlike the dropped v0.59.0 resume: a fork replays the SOURCE's pinned config (pinned_flat, train_campaign.py:366) and v0.62.0's config.json is already post-throughput-work -- async_actors 48, actor_games 4, drain_per_cycle 256, traj_queue_size 2048, checkpoint_every 10000, idle window 17-7. Seed stays 1, inherited from v0.62.0; that is correct, this is a continuation of that trajectory, not a new sample. INTERPRETATION LIMIT: n=1 against a measured 28-Elo seed spread on this recipe (v0.60.0 814 / v0.62.0 842), so only a gain beyond ~30 Elo is evidence. To separate 'annealing helped' from 'restarting at the peak on fresher data helped', add the matched control -- the same fork with rnad.lr_schedule=constant to the same 90k horizon -- as a second arm; it is deliberately NOT included here so this run owns the box tonight. TIMING: 60k steps at v0.62.0's measured 2.87 steps/s = 10,350 steps/h -> ~5.8h. Forks auto-version at the requested bump, so this lands as the next free minor (v0.63.0) and leaves v0.62.0 untouched on disk.
runs.name: tf-wsd-from-v0.62-peak

runs._comment: RUN 2 -- long-horizon extension of the GRU v0.41.0 (lr 1e-4, eta 0.5, batch 32) from 240k to 500k. Carried over from the previous revision, with the idle-window restatement added (see below). Rationale: v0.41.0 was still IMPROVING when its previous horizon ran out -- Elo 666 @190k -> 691 @210k -> 693 @220k -> 695 @240k -- so 240k was a schedule limit, not a plateau. lr SCHEDULE: a resume replays v0.41.0's PINNED config.json as its base, and that file still records the ORIGINAL 80k run (lr 1e-4, no lr_schedule/lr_warmup/lr_min keys at all -> 'constant', idle window 19-6); the wsd schedule and 17-7 window of the 80k->240k extension live only in that extension's sweep entry, NOT on disk. VERIFIED 2026-08-11 against checkpoints/v0.41.0/config.json: still no lr_schedule/lr_warmup/lr_min keys, still train_start_hour 19 / train_stop_hour 6, so every restatement below is load-bearing. Restated as cosine over the FULL 0->500k horizon instead of continuing the old wsd: the previous segment annealed all the way down to lr_min=1e-5 by 240k, and 260k further steps at 1e-5 would buy almost nothing. Because lr_at_step derives lr from the absolute step, cosine(0->500k) resumes at ~5.8e-5 -- a mild warm restart, still well under the 1e-4 peak -- then anneals smoothly back to 1e-5 at 500k. Note this restart is a genuine lr discontinuity (1e-5 -> 5.8e-5 at the resume step); it is the intended cost of extending an already-annealed run, and the alternative (wsd holding a flat 1e-4 until 340k) restarts 10x harder. IDLE WINDOW NOW ACTUALLY RESTATED: the previous revision's comment asserted the 17-7 window 'must be restated here', but its overrides only carried the three lr keys, so under --honour-idle this run would have inherited the pinned 19-6 and trained a 2h-shorter night than intended. train.train_start_hour/train_stop_hour are added below to close that gap. It is moot under the campaign's default IGNORE_IDLE=True (train_campaign.py:108, which exports DEEPNASH_IGNORE_IDLE=1 to every run) and only takes effect if you pass --honour-idle; it is set correctly either way. Note this run does NOT inherit 'defaults' (resumes never do), so the batch=64 / transformer settings above cannot leak into it, and the actor knobs are deliberately left at v0.41.0's pinned values -- unlike run 1 this is a same-recipe extension whose whole value is comparability against its own 190k-240k curve. TIMING: 260k steps at v0.41.0's measured ~14,150 steps/h over its 80k->240k segment is ~18h of learner time, and it starts only after run 1, so it spans the following night.
runs.name: gru-v0.41-to-500k-cosine
